## Linear Algebra: Theory and Applications

This is the course website for **MATH 332 — Fall 2026 Section 002** at Illinois
Institute of Technology.

## Course Description

This course develops the theory and applications of linear algebra through
systems of equations, matrices, determinants, vector spaces, eigenvalues and
eigenvectors, and inner product spaces. Python will support visualization,
numerical computation, symbolic computation, and experimentation.

{{< include classlib/classlib/quarto/snippets/fred-hickernell-bio.qmd >}}

## Required course materials

- **WileyPLUS access:** WileyPLUS is required for this course. All homework
  will be assigned, completed individually, and automatically graded through
  WileyPLUS. Launch each homework assignment from
  [Canvas]({{< meta canvas.course >}}).
- **Textbook:** Howard Anton, *Elementary Linear Algebra: Applications
  Version*, 12th edition. Single-term WileyPLUS access includes the online
  textbook for the duration of the course, so a separate printed copy is
  optional. See [Resources](pages/resources.qmd) for details.

To read the online textbook without opening a homework assignment, open
[Wiley Course Resources in Canvas]({{< meta canvas.wiley_resources >}}),
select **Course Resources**, and click **Launch** beside
**WileyPLUS eTextbook**. Use the **Practice** tab for additional practice. See
[Wiley's illustrated access instructions](https://wpsupport.wiley.com/s/article/How-to-Access-the-WileyPLUS-eTextbook-in-Canvas).
If **Wiley Course Resources** is missing from your course menu, let the
instructor know.

## Course Outline

<details>
<summary><strong>Why Linear Algebra?</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/00-why-linear-algebra.html). Course motivation and roadmap.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Systems of Linear Equations and Matrices</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/01-systems-and-matrices.html). Anton, Chapter 1. Detailed pacing is **TBD**.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Inverses and Invertibility</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/02-inverses-and-invertibility.html). Anton, Chapter 1. Detailed pacing is **TBD**.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Matrix Structure and Transformations</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/03-matrix-structure-and-transformations.html). Anton, Chapter 1. Detailed pacing is **TBD**.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Determinants</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/04-determinants.html). Anton, Chapter 2. Detailed pacing is **TBD**.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Euclidean Vector Spaces</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/05-euclidean-vector-spaces.html). Anton, Chapter 3. Detailed pacing is **TBD**.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Vector Spaces, Subspaces, and Span</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/06-general-vector-spaces.html). Anton §§4.1–4.3:
real vector spaces, subspaces, and spanning sets. Detailed pacing is **TBD**.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Bases, Dimension, and Coordinates</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/07-bases-dimension-and-coordinates.html). Anton §§4.4–4.7:
linear independence, coordinates and basis, dimension, and change of basis.
Extracting a basis by elimination also connects to §4.8. Frames and infinite
algebraic bases are enrichment; complex dimension and coordinate isomorphisms
preview §§5.3 and 8.3. Detailed pacing is **TBD**.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Matrix Spaces and Rank</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/08-matrix-spaces-and-rank.html). Anton §§4.8–4.9:
row, column, and null spaces; rank, nullity, and the fundamental matrix spaces.
The closing examples of abstract linear transformations and their matrices
preview §§8.1 and 8.4. Detailed pacing is **TBD**.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/09-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.html). Anton, Chapter 5. Detailed pacing is **TBD**.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Inner Product Spaces</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/10-inner-product-spaces.html). Anton, Chapter 6:
inner products, orthogonal projection, Gram–Schmidt and QR, least squares and
regression, and function approximation with Fourier coordinates.
Detailed pacing is **TBD**.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Special Topics</strong></summary>

[Lecture slides](slides/11-special-topics.html). A draft capstone: SVD and
regression, quadratic forms, FFT, tensor products, and network applications.
Selected Anton Chapters 7–10 plus supplementary Fourier and tensor material.
Topics and pacing will be selected as time permits.

</details>

## Assessment

- [**Homework assignments:**](pages/assignments.qmd) 20%; all homework
  assignments are completed individually through WileyPLUS
- [**Quizzes: 15%**](pages/quizzes-and-tests.qmd); see the linked quiz and test
  schedule for dates and coverage
- [**Tests: 25%**](pages/quizzes-and-tests.qmd); see the linked quiz and test
  schedule for dates and coverage
- [**Final Exam: 40%**](pages/quizzes-and-tests.qmd); _on the date assigned by
  the registrar_
- **Extra Credit:** From August 24 through December 6, you may earn extra
  credit by being the first student to report a previously unreported error in

  - my lecture slides, Jupyter notebooks, or assignments at least 24 hours
    after the material was presented or posted; or
  - the textbook.

  Report each error by creating an [issue](https://github.com/fjhickernell/MATH332Fall2026/issues)
  in the course repository. Each confirmed error earns 0.5 or 1 percentage
  point, depending on the severity of the error, up to 10 percentage points
  total.

  Extra credit is added to your final weighted course total. *Canvas may not
  display the weighted total correctly until grades have been recorded in
  every assessment category.*
